The noon report nr-0102 for MV TORMAR SPRING (SIM-0002) was checked against the charter party warranty:

- Reported VLSFO consumption: 27.6 t
- Warranted VLSFO consumption: 24.0 t/day
- Excess: 15.0% (beyond the 10% tolerance the desk accepts)
- Avg speed: 12.5 kn vs warranted 12.5 kn (speed is on warranty)

2. Alert the operator that the day shows 27.6 t VLSFO consumed against a warranted 24 t/day (15% excess) on a good-weather day, so it stands as a potential warranty deviation.

detail.text: Summary for the operator: The noon report nr-0104 for MV TORMAR SPRING (SIM-0002) was extracted cleanly with no missing figures. The Master's ETA of 2025-01-31 0300 UTC to Sept-Iles is consistent with the distance and basis speed, and no charter party ETA notice is due at this time. However, the ECMWF forecast puts arrival at 2025-01-31 2048 UTC — 17.8 hours after the Master's ETA, beyond the CP's 12-hour change limit — so the ETA is at risk. VLSFO consumption of 28.3 t/day versus the 24 t/day warranty was flagged, but heavy weather (Beaufort 10, Douglas 8) explains it and the day is excluded from the warranty assessment; a voyage note was filed. I have put one decision on your desk: whether to ask the Master to review the ETA in view of the forecast. Nothing has been sent yet.

Dear Master,

Please review the Sept-Iles ETA in view of the ECMWF forecast, which gives a forecast ETA of 2025-01-31 2048 UTC — 17.8 hours after your ETA of 2025-01-31 0300 UTC — exceeding the charter party's 12-hour ETA change limit.

No notice will be issued on the forecast ETA. We kindly ask you to review and respond at your earliest convenience.

Best regards,
